correctness.rationale: The local criterion was independently reconstructed in part-count variables: for an outside vertex in part \(i\), a valid geodesic triple with two selected vertices exists exactly when either the selected set meets its part and at least one other part, or some other part contributes at least two selected vertices. This criterion gives the stated minimum-number cases and exhausts all minimum sets: the whole graph for a complete graph, cross-part pairs plus two-vertex whole parts in the bipartite case, whole two-vertex parts for at least three parts, and otherwise the three listed size-three patterns. Independent brute force on every complete multipartite type through order nine reproduced both the minimum and the exact minimum-set count for 87 types.
